title: The alumni mentor wants to “help your credit”
scenario: An alumnus you met through a networking group offers to help you build credit by adding you to a special financial account. They need your ID, social-security/tax number and a small setup fee.

answers.A: Share only the ID first because the mentor came through a legitimate university group.
answers.B: Do not provide the data; verify the person and any financial product independently through regulated providers or university career/alumni channels.
answers.C: Ask for the product name and written terms, then review them with a trusted financial adviser or family member.

explanation: Real networks can be used to manufacture trust. Identity data should not be exchanged for vague financial shortcuts.
proTip: A warm introduction does not make a financial product safe.
